Definition: properly, to be smooth, i.e. (by implication) to escape (as if by slipperiness); causatively, to release or rescue; specifically, to bring forth young, emit sparks
BiblicalUsage: Malat means to escape, to slip away, to be delivered, and it is the word for getting out alive. Genesis 19:17 has the angel telling Lot, escape for thy life, look not behind thee, and Psalms 124:7 says our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers. Daniel 12:1 promises thy people shall be delivered, every one found written in the book, and Joel 2:32 says whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the whole gospel in a verb: escape is not something I manage, it is something God gives. My position is that Joel 2:32 is the open door in all four verses, because calling on the name of the LORD is the one escape that never fails.
